description: 1996 Ford Mustang SVT Cobra Coupe For Sale in Rare "Mystic!"  1-Owner Since New  Completely Stock  Only 60K Miles  WE FINANCE  Every once in a while, a car comes through our doors that makes us realize we may not get another opportunity quite like it.  This is one of those cars.  Finished in the legendary Mystic Clearcoat Metallic over Black leather, this 1996 Ford Mustang SVT Cobra is already part of an extremely special chapter in Mustang history. Ford produced only 2,000 Mystic Cobras for 1996, wearing one of the most recognizable color-shifting factory finishes of the era.  But that's not what makes this particular car extraordinary.  This Cobra has had ONE owner since 1996.  The original owner purchased it new, garage kept it, maintained it, and preserved it for nearly three decades. Today it remains completely stock and unmodified, shows only 60,000 original miles, and carries a Clean Carfax with no accident history.  In a world where most surviving SN95 Cobras have passed through numerous owners, been modified, returned to stock, or simply lived very different lives, finding one with this combination of provenance and originality is remarkable.   One Owner Since 1996  Finding a Mystic Cobra isn't impossible. Finding one that's still stock, accident-free, well maintained, and showing reasonable mileage gets considerably harder.  Finding one still coming from the person who bought it new nearly 30 years ago is something else entirely.  This isn't a multi-owner Cobra that someone eventually returned to stock. It isn't a modified car wearing enough factory pieces to look original in photographs.  It has simply remained stock.  One owner purchased it new, garage kept it, maintained it, and resisted something that became almost irresistible with these cars: modifying it.  That's an entirely different kind of preservation.   Mystic  For 1996, Ford offered the SVT Cobra in the incredible Mystic Clearcoat Metallic, a color-shifting finish that dramatically changes depending on lighting and viewing angle.  Blue / Purple / Green / Bronze  It was outrageous in 1996 and remains one of the most recognizable factory finishes ever applied to a Mustang. Only 2,000 SVT Cobras received Mystic paint, making these cars special from the very beginning.   The Beginning Of The Modular Cobra  1996 marked the arrival of Ford's new modular V8 architecture in the Mustang, but SVT didn't simply install the GT's version.  The Cobra received a 4.6-liter DOHC 32-valve V8 producing 305 horsepower and 300 lb-ft of torque, paired with a proper manual transmission and rear-wheel drive.  These engines were special pieces in their own right, assembled using two-person teams with each engine built from start to finish before being signed off.  It was a completely different personality from the pushrod Cobras that preceded it and represented the beginning of an engine lineage that would become enormously important to Ford performance. You can hunt down original wheels, exhaust, suspension, stereo equipment, and all the other pieces that disappeared from these cars over the years.  What you cannot recreate is nearly 30 years of single-owner provenance.  This car has been driven, maintained, serviced, and enjoyed while remaining remarkably faithful to exactly what Ford and SVT built in 1996.  One owner. 60,000 original miles. Clean history. Garage kept. And completely unmodified.  That's what makes this one different.   The 1996 Mystic Cobra was special when it was new. Time has only made finding the right one considerably harder.  With only 2,000 originally finished in Mystic Clearcoat Metallic, these cars already occupy a special place in SVT history. This example adds something production numbers can't adequately describe: nearly three decades of uninterrupted single-owner history and preservation.  We've had rarer cars. We've had lower-mile cars.  But finding a nearly 30-year-old performance Mustang in a highly collectible factory specification that is still stock, still accident-free, still showing only 60k miles, and coming directly from its original owner? OVERVIEW The 1990 Porsche 911 Reimagined by Singer is the kind of car that blurs the line between restoration and modern performance machine. Starting with a 964-generation 911, Singer strips the car down to its core and rebuilds it with modern engineering, hand-finished details, and a level of craftsmanship that turns an already iconic Porsche into something completely bespoke. This particular example is a Turbo Study, born in May 2025 and meticulously maintained. The heart of this build is a 3.8-liter twin-turbocharged flat-six, paired with a manual transmission. Unlike a factory 964 Turbo, the engine and supporting systems have been completely reworked as part of Singer's Turbo Study program. The result is a powertrain designed to deliver the punch of a modern turbocharged Porsche while keeping the direct connection and mechanical character of a manual 911. This example is listed with a rear-wheel-drive layout, keeping the driving experience focused on the driver. The chassis receives the same level of attention. Singer's approach goes far beyond cosmetic restoration, with the original 964 being stripped down and re-engineered before being rebuilt. Carbon-fiber bodywork helps reduce weight, while upgraded suspension, brakes, steering, and other mechanical systems are designed to give the car modern levels of control without losing the feel that made the air-cooled 911 so special. Visually, the car captures the timeless shape of the classic 911 while Singer's custom bodywork and carefully reshaped details create a presence that is vintage and modern. The interior takes the same approach. The cabin combines classic design cues with modern materials and hand craftsmanship. Bespoke leather, paint matched trim, custom gauges, and a period-inspired dashboard deliver an interior that feels special and nostalgic. The Porsche 911 by Singer is ultimately about one idea: taking the revered air-cooled 964 and asking what it could become with virtually no compromises. With a twin-turbo flat-six, manual transmission, carbon-fiber construction, and bespoke Singer engineering it becomes a completely reimagined interpretation of one of the world's greatest driver's cars.
